stem: When conversing in person with a person who communicates through a sign language interpreter, which behavior conforms to proper disability etiquette?

options.text: Ask the interpreter whether the person needs any other communication support.
options.shortLabel: Ask the interpreter about the person's needs
options.rationale: Routing questions about the person's communication needs through the interpreter excludes the person from the conversation; ask the person directly.

options.text: Direct your gaze toward the interpreter while they sign, then turn to the person when responding.
options.shortLabel: Alternate gaze between interpreter and person
options.rationale: Although following the interpretation is important, directing attention primarily toward the interpreter rather than the person can interfere with direct interpersonal communication.

options.text: Maintain direct eye contact with the person and speak directly to them.
options.shortLabel: Look and speak directly to the person
options.rationale: Proper etiquette requires looking at and addressing the individual directly, acknowledging their presence and autonomy.

options.text: Check with the interpreter that the person has understood your remarks.
options.rationale: Checking comprehension with the interpreter rather than the person treats the interpreter as a go-between and excludes the person from the exchange.

explanation: When communicating through an interpreter, speak directly to the person and maintain direct eye contact with them. The interpreter facilitates interpretation as a neutral conduit; do not route questions or comprehension checks through the interpreter.

references.title: IAAP CPACC Body of Knowledge v4.0
references.author: IAAP
